code: UA_ByteString msg = UA_ByteString(); UA_ByteString_allocBuffer(&msg, size); memcpy(msg.data, data, size);
note: Fuzzer input bytes are copied into a UA_ByteString message buffer that will be passed to the server for binary message processing.
The attacker-controlled binary message is handed to the OPC UA server for chunk processing and service dispatch.

code: UA_StatusCode retval = UA_Connection_processChunks(connection, server, processCompleteChunk, message);
note: The raw message bytes are parsed as OPC UA TCP chunks; a valid HEL/OPN handshake and a service request chunk are required to reach service dispatch.
A complete chunk is dispatched to the secure channel processor, which decodes the OPC UA binary message and routes it to the service handler.
An AddNodes request item is decoded from the binary message; a new node is allocated from the nodestore for the requested node class.

The requested new NodeId is copied into the freshly allocated node. If the source NodeId has an invalid or uninitialized identifierType, the copy may leave the destination nodeId's identifier fields in an inconsistent state.
The browse name is copied; if the previous copy failed, retval is non-zero and the node is deleted via UA_Nodestore_delete.
When any copy or attribute-setting step fails, the partially-initialized node is passed to UA_Nodestore_delete, which invokes UA_Node_deleteMembers on the node.

The node's nodeId member is deleted. If the nodeId's identifierType field or its string identifier fields were not properly initialized (e.g., due to a failed copy or a malformed decoded NodeId), this reads uninitialized memory.

code: switch(p->identifierType) { case UA_NODEIDTYPE_STRING: case UA_NODEIDTYPE_BYTESTRING: String_deleteMembers(&p->identifier.string, NULL); }
note: The identifierType field is read to decide which identifier member to free. If identifierType is uninitialized or points to a string whose length/data fields are uninitialized, String_deleteMembers reads uninitialized values, causing the use-of-uninitialized-value crash.
